findings.what: In every mode except 'r', only the horizontal driver (mapR) comes from the selected field; the vertical driver is always the map's green channel. §13 names mapR and mapG verbatim, so mode 'r' is exact, but for luma/hue/g/b 'mode selects mapR, green always supplies mapG' — one of two plausible readings.
findings.why: The card lists modes next to a formula using mapR and mapG as distinct channels; it never says the mode field also becomes mapG. Verified: a pure-red map in mode 'hue' shifts BOTH axes (hue=0 for x, G=0 for y).
findings.fix: None required — docstring documents the reading, all five accepts hold. If the human prefers 'mode replaces the whole map (monoplan -> both axes)', one-line change in _sample_coordinates' call site, but a contract clarification, not a defect.

findings.what: mask keyword-only because EffectFn is Callable[[Image,dict,Generator],Image] and EffectInstance/PipelineSpec carry no mask field (preset.py:40 partial bridge). pipeline._apply_effects calls fn(out, params, rng) and can never pass a mask, so in pipeline use the mask is always None.
findings.why: §18 says every glitch effect accepts a mask; displace accepts one (keyword-only) but it is only mask-reachable via direct API calls.
findings.fix: Acceptable as-is (E3/E1). Optionally converge on one mechanism when a card owns the EffectInstance schema (note: pixel_sort aligned to keyword-only per DEV-214, so both now consistent).

findings.what: map_source 'sequence' and 'feedback' are indistinguishable: both read the same caller-supplied map_img kwarg (E1a). The pipeline never passes map_img, so neither source is reachable from a PipelineSpec — only from direct calls.
findings.why: EffectFn has no channel to distinguish a sequence frame from a feedback-buffer snapshot, so sharing one argument loses no semantics the core can express.
findings.fix: None — declared E1, reasonable. A future bridge/animation card can supply map_img and the distinction becomes meaningful at the call site.

regression: none — full suite re-run by me: 1811 passed, 1 skipped (includes L14's 80 owned tests). The diff is additive (new displace.py, new test_displace.py, one import line). No previously-working behavior changed.

tests_that_cannot_fail: The discriminating accepts are covered by the ramp, smear-growth, mask-ones, distinct-modes, bilinear, clamp and noise-seeding tests, each mutation-killed (sign flip, nearest sampling, inverted mask, no clamp — all detected).
notes: All five accept items verified by my own execution: flat grey map bit-identical across 5 modes x iterations 1/3/8; horizontal ramp with neutral green driver shifts exactly -k/2/+k/2 at saturated extremes (interior exact k*(mapR-0.5)); edge spread 0 -> 9 px from iterations 1 -> 3; mask zeros bit-identical, mask ones bit-identical to unmasked, half-mask = midpoint; output shape/dtype/range hold for 5 modes x 5 shapes incl. (1,1); bilinear half-pixel and edge clamp confirmed. E1 adjudications: (a) sequence|feedback sharing map_img is sound. (b) The coder's note is wrong about its own code: a monoplan map IS promoted to R=G=B and drives BOTH axes diagonally (verified: monoplan ramp, out[32,10]==src[28,6], not src[32,6]); the 'ramp ±k/2' accept still holds because the test source is y-constant, and driving both axes is the literal reading of §13's two-channel formula — the correct interpretation.
